docs.title: RustMT4 SDK
docs.text: Welcome to the RustMT4 SDK documentation. This high-performance asynchronous Rust crate connects directly to MetaTrader 4 servers without requiring a local desktop terminal or Wine.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Memory Safety & Performance: Built purely in safe, modern Rust.
  • Asynchronous Tokio Engine: Non-blocking channel streams for ticks and order responses.
  • Complete Order Lifecycle: Market execution, pending limit/stop orders, SL/TP modify, and position closing.
  • Type-Safe Models: Strongly typed structs and enums with Serde serialization.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Rust Application] -->|Tokio Async Socket| B[MT4Client]
    B -->|Encrypted Protocol| C[MetaTrader 4 Server]
    C -->|Price Feeds| B
    C -->|Order Confirmations| B
    B -->|mpsc::Receiver<Quote>| A

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text:
Add to your Cargo.toml:

[dependencies]
metarpc-mt4 = { git = "https://github.com/MetaRPC/RustMT4.git" }
tokio = { version = "1.38", features = ["full"] }

See Getting Started to build your first strategy.

docs.title: MT4Client Methods
docs.text:
• pub fn new(host: impl Into<String>, port: u16) -> Self
  • pub async fn connect(&mut self, login: u64, password: &str) -> Result<(), MT4Error>
  • pub async fn disconnect(&mut self)
  • pub fn is_connected(&self) -> bool
  • pub async fn get_account_info(&self) -> Result<AccountInfo, MT4Error>
  • pub async fn subscribe_quotes(&self, symbols: Vec<String>) -> Result<mpsc::Receiver<Quote>, MT4Error>
  • pub async fn order_send(&self, req: OrderRequest) -> Result<OrderResult, MT4Error>
  • pub async fn order_modify(&self, ticket: u64, sl: f64, tp: f64) -> Result<(), MT4Error>
  • pub async fn order_close(&self, ticket: u64, lots: f64) -> Result<(), MT4Error>

docs.title: Connection & Authentication
docs.text:
Managing connections with MT4Client.

use metarpc_mt4::MT4Client;

let mut client = MT4Client::new("demo.broker.com", 443);
client.connect(100234, "password").await?;

if client.is_connected() {
    println!("Connected and authenticated!");
}

client.disconnect().await;

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::{MT4Client, OrderRequest, OrderType};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut client = MT4Client::new("mt4.broker.com", 443);

    client.connect(100234, "account_pass").await?;
    println!("Connected to MT4!");

    let acc = client.get_account_info().await?;
    println!("Account Balance: {} {}", acc.balance, acc.currency);

    // Send 0.01 lot Buy
    let req = OrderRequest {
        symbol: "EURUSD".to_string(),
        order_type: OrderType::Buy,
        lots: 0.01,
        price: None,
        stop_loss: None,
        take_profit: None,
        slippage: Some(30),
        comment: Some("Rust Quickstart".to_string()),
    };

    let result = client.order_send(req).await?;
    println!("Order sent! Ticket #{}", result.ticket);

    Ok(())
}

docs.title: Quotes & Market Data
docs.text:
Receiving tick streams with Tokio channels:

let mut quote_rx = client.subscribe_quotes(vec!["EURUSD".to_string()]).await?;

while let Some(quote) = quote_rx.recv().await {
    println!("[{}] Bid: {} | Ask: {}", quote.symbol, quote.bid, quote.ask);
}

docs.title: Trading & Orders
docs.text:
Placing, modifying, and closing orders.

// Open Order
let order = client.order_send(OrderRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    order_type: OrderType::Buy,
    lots: 0.1,
    price: None,
    stop_loss: Some(1.0800),
    take_profit: Some(1.0950),
    slippage: Some(10),
    comment: Some("Algo Trade".into()),
}).await?;

// Modify SL/TP
client.order_modify(order.ticket, 1.0820, 1.0960).await?;

// Close Order
client.order_close(order.ticket, 0.1).await?;
